title: Why does airport security swab your hands?

record.question: Why does airport security swab your hands?
record.audience_reason: Millions fly home this Thanksgiving weekend and many get a hand swab with no explanation; the answer is a hidden chemistry instrument most people never picture, and swab explainers are breaking out on TikTok and Instagram this month.

editorial_contribution.statement: We follow one invisible speck of residue all the way through a simplified ion mobility trace detector, built from NIST and DHS descriptions: swab, heated desorber, ion source, a drift-tube race against a gas headwind, an arrival-time trace in milliseconds, and the library check that decides alarm or no alarm.

record.custom_scene: On a blueprint world, a generic hand is wiped by a swab on a wand and yellow specks hop onto the pad; a magnifier shows a fingertip with residue that the swab lifts; a cutaway detector takes the swab, its heater coils glow while a desorber gauge fills and the speck rises as vapor; vapor molecules pass a small ion source and come out ringed with charge; in a drift tube a gate opens and three kinds of ions race to a detector plate while gas streaks flow back; an arrival-time trace sweeps 0-15 ms and the yellow peak is flagged as the fingerprint; two mini traces show a library match (red light) and no match (green light).

cover_composition.main_object: open hand mid-swab with glowing residue specks and a magnifier on a fingertip

record.sources_and_assumptions: See sources-and-rights.md. Assumptions: the detector is a generic, simplified ion mobility spectrometer (TSA's deployed contact-sampling ETDs are IMS-based per DHS S&T 2022; newer mass-spectrometry ETDs exist and are not shown); the three peaks and their times are illustrative, labeled on screen; no desorber temperature is stated (only one source, NIST IR 7240, gave a range, so it was cut); 'usually' a radioactive source per NIST (nickel-63) and ASU; we say nothing about who gets swabbed or how often (no sourced claim), and nothing that could help anyone avoid detection.
